sources.note: ADB-Japan Scholarship Program main page on adb.org (the awarding body's own site). States programme scope, fully-funded coverage, general eligibility, and the graduate/master's level.

Official 'Procedures for Applying' sub-page. Confirms there is no separate application to ADB and that applications go to the chosen academic institution at least six (6) months before the intended intake.

awarding_body.detail: The page is ADB's own (adb.org, titled 'Asian Development Bank') and states the programme is financed by the Government of Japan, matching the record's awarding body.
awarding_body.quote: Since April 1988, with financing from the Government of Japan, we have offered citizens from developing member countries of ADB the opportunity to pursue graduate studies in 27 selected educational institutions across Asia and the Pacific, including 17 in Japan.

deadline.detail: As the record states, there is no single ADB deadline; the application goes to the chosen academic institution at least six months before the intended start of studies. Precision 'varies' is correct and there is no exact calendar date to record because intake deadlines are set per Designated Institution. No past/closed deadline is shown, so it is not blocked as closed.
deadline.quote: The duly accomplished applications form together with all copies of academic records should be sent to the institution at least six (6) months before the commencement of the intake that you wish to join.

eligibility.detail: The record carries no eligibility_summary, so there are no specific eligibility claims to contradict; the page's requirements are consistent with the Master's-level record. For reference the page requires national of an ADB borrowing member country, admission to an approved master's course, a bachelor's degree, and at least two years of full-time work experience.
eligibility.quote: Be a national of an ADB borrowing member country and Japanese ODA scholarship-eligible country. ... Have gained admission to an approved master's course at a Designated Institution. Hold a bachelor's degree or its equivalent with superior academic record.

funding.detail: Confirmed Fully Funded, not tuition-only: full tuition plus monthly subsistence, books, medical insurance and travel are provided, with a possible thesis grant. Note the page also lists material exclusions (family expenses, extra-curricular courses, additional travel, supplementary materials/field trips/workshops, and computers).
funding.quote: The ADB-Japan Scholarship Program provides: Full tuition fees; Monthly subsistence allowance (including housing); Books and instructional materials; Medical insurance; Travel expenses

degree_levels.detail: Master's / graduate. The page describes graduate scholarships and requires admission to an approved master's course, matching the record's Master's level.
degree_levels.quote: The ADB-Japan Scholarship Program (JSP) offers about 130 graduate scholarships a year for studies in economics, business and management, science and technology, and other development-related fields.

recommended_field_updates.deadline_text: Applications should be sent to the institution at least six (6) months before the commencement of the intake you wish to join. No separate application to ADB is necessary; apply to your chosen academic institution, which sets its own intake deadline.
recommended_field_updates.verification_notes: Read adb.org main page and the 'Procedures for Applying' sub-page on 2026-10-12. Ongoing programme with no single ADB deadline; intake deadlines are set per Designated Institution, so re-checks should confirm the specific institution's intake date each cycle. Award is fully funded (tuition + monthly subsistence + books + insurance + travel) but expressly excludes family expenses, extra-curricular courses, additional travel during the program, supplementary materials/field trips/workshops, and computers (see the Procedures-for-Applying 'Important to note').
